images.title: A kite from diagonals 6 cm and 8 cm
images.purpose: Shows the kite built from diagonals AC = 6 cm and BD = 8 cm, where BD cuts AC in half at right angles but O is not the middle of BD.
images.composition: Plain white background, the main object large and centred with wide empty margins, no scenery, no characters, no extra decoration. Two crossing diagonals in the centre with their ends joined into a kite.
images.exact_structure: A thick teal (#0072B2) horizontal segment AC and a thick amber (#E69F00) vertical segment BD crossing at O. A small filled reddish purple (#CC79A7) square right angle mark at O. O is the midpoint of AC: each half of AC carries one short tick mark and is labelled 3 cm. O is not the midpoint of BD: the upper part OB is short, labelled 2 cm, and the lower part OD is long, labelled 6 cm. The four ends are joined in order A, B, C, D by thin dashed grey (#6B7280) lines, making a kite with the short pair of sides at the top. The letters A, B, C, D sit just outside the ends, A at the left, B at the top, C at the right, D at the bottom. No side lengths. Nothing else in the frame.
rejection: any count of objects, cells, ticks or rows that differs from the numbers stated in the spec
any text beyond the listed visible text, or any listed text misspelled or altered
any board name, publisher name, book title, page number or curriculum branding anywhere in the frame
a hyphen used in place of a minus sign on any labelled number
images.takeaway: In a kite one diagonal cuts the other in half at right angles; the other diagonal need not be cut in half.
images.description: Shows the kite built from diagonals AC = 6 cm and BD = 8 cm, where BD cuts AC in half at right angles but O is not the middle of BD.
images.context: Any split of BD other than 4 and 4 gives a kite that is not a rhombus; 2 + 6 = 8.

image_decisions.why: The construction this practice asks for, with the unequal split of BD made visible.
